notes: The fitting cases use document tolerance 1e-5 for each independent fitted result.

Preserved curves and surfaces retain the Rust source degrees and full knots exactly. Native control positions and knot values use 1e-11; independent line-length domains can differ by approximately 2e-15.
Complete preserved NURBS structure, sampled curves and faces, solid box incidence, mesh colors, names, groups, selection, Undo and Redo are checked.
Native groups are normalized to retained object-table indices for comparing membership; UUID ordering is not compared.
Repeated Copy batches create geometry from original sources and share one Undo entry; zero angles create no objects.
The command cases do not establish arbitrary trimmed-surface, continuous fitting error or full Rhino compatibility.
Native RhinoCommon mesh alpha is opacity; regression setup converts it to the kernel/OpenNURBS transparency convention. Retained raw observations are unchanged.

32 bounded native commands were captured entirely in a private Xvfb with an owned settings scheme, pointer path, snapshot acknowledgement and framebuffer crop. Each command first primes remembered scalar input to zero.
Temporary previews leave source geometry and undo history unchanged. They draw object-colored wires/points over original selected sources; original shaded/ghosted faces remain.

Standalone curves elevated to at least cubic degree reproduce measured temporary cages even with PreserveStructure enabled. Low-degree polynomial surfaces and B-rep edges interpolate mapped Greville samples in cubic space. Preserved surfaces and single-face B-rep edges map original controls. These display approximations skip adaptive fitting.
An axial cursor retains the last valid preview. An 81-step mouse path establishes 450 degrees independently of the endpoint principal angle; normal paths have 17 steps.

Raw public QuickPreview and degree-elevated SDK outputs, pending snapshots and completed geometry are retained. Box wires compare against rows/columns of public QuickPreview patch grids, allowing independent UV orientations. One supplementary capture retains all 12 public QuickPreview B-rep edges, with independently normalized order and direction.

Line pixel witnesses use five positions, a 3-pixel neighborhood and RGB tolerance 25 (at least four hits per capture). Surface witnesses use 21 interior boundary/isocurve samples and a 2-pixel distance to RGB within 8 of the object color (at least 19 hits). Box patches use 540 path samples with the same color/distance rule and at least 85 percent hits. Two source-face interiors check retained selected-face color. Checksums preserve every PNG; this is not a pixel-identical comparison.
An explicit offscreen test on NVIDIA GB10/Vulkan driver 610.57.04 passes in linear and sRGB target formats, checking overlay visibility over opaque faces and world clipping.

Rational and higher-degree surfaces use mapped controls as display approximations; their native preview policy, arbitrary-shape preview parity, continuous fitting bounds and end-to-end performance are not established by these witnesses.

scope: Independent public TwistSpaceMorph point maps and actual Twist command captures in an owned private Xvfb Rhino session. No proprietary source was inspected.

notes: The Rust probe is a native release build; both helpers preconstruct source points and warm up before timing batches.
Rhino performs public MorphPoint calls and coordinate extraction through Python/RhinoCommon on FEX/Wine. Its source morph construction, startup and JSON transport are outside the timing loop.
Rust times point mapping and collection into an owned coordinate vector. This differs from the Rhino Python/CLR route.
The exported ratios compare harness elapsed time and cannot establish a native Rhino kernel speedup.
